answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to anchor a verifiable work history before it can trade: a newcomer must complete a supervised voyage of small, attested tasks whose results are checked by established peers, building a reputation trail that is costly to fake in bulk. Like a cedar that grows slowly and cannot be cloned overnight, trust should accumulate over time, so a single operator spinning up thousands of fresh identities still faces the summit of proving real, sustained work for each one before any of them earns weight.
